item.title: Nex 2.7.1
item.description: Pinch works on shelves. Arranged by kind or tag, a pinch now folds every shelf and a spread opens them all, as it does with days. The list also holds still while two fingers are on it, so a pinch no longer scrolls the page away under your fingers. Tidier shelf headings. The fold arrow sits in the same place on every heading, and in Persian it points the way you read. Opening See all , coming back, choosing a filter or another arrangement now fades the list in instead of cutting to it. Older dates in the date picker. Choosing a year and a month in the Persian calendar now moves the selected day with them, so a date like 27 Bahman 1365 can be set without hunting for the day first. Converter reads dates the way you write them. Besides 1365/11/27, the date field accepts the day first (27/11/1365) and month names (۲۷ بهمن ۱۳۶۵, 16 Feb 1987), and a number written as ۲/۵ reads as two and a half. Recent keeps only real conversions. Switching tabs, calendars, categories or charts no longer fills Recent with default values; a date or number you type is kept once, even while you are still correcting it. The vault asks for what you set. With Fingerprint or biometrics on, opening a private tool asks for your fingerprint or face alone, as the app lock does; cancelling the prompt is no longer shown as an error. A locked vault leaves nothing open. When the vault locks — by its timer, by the app lock or after time away — a private photo open full screen and a recording in progress close with it, the privacy cover now covers them too, and decrypted copies of attachments are cleared. A password you copied is wiped when the vault hides, and a password shown in the editor hides itself again after a few seconds. Private attachments always open. Two attachments added at the very first moment the vault was used could seal one of them under a key that was then replaced, leaving it unreadable. Both now share one key. A quicker, sturdier start. Opening asks the system less and no longer queues the library's bookkeeping in front of the database, so the timeline is ready sooner. If the library ever fails to open, Try again starts clean, and a file that never answers can no longer keep a restart waiting. Lighter in the background. With the on-device search model installed, going behind another app now releases it, as the assistant's model already was, so the system has less reason to close Nex while you are elsewhere. Lighter, safer attachments. Picking several photos onto a note no longer loads each one whole into memory, a voice clip recorded onto a note is saved straight into the library — so a save that fails no longer loses the recording — and sharing a photo with no location in it sends the original file.

item.title: Nex 2.7.0
item.description: Group the home screen by kind or by tag. Besides time, the home screen can now sort notes onto shelves by what they are — writing, checklists, voice, photos, links, files — or by tag, so a note is found by what you remember about it. Each shelf shows its newest six and how many it holds, See all opens the rest, and shelves can be moved up or down. Choose it in the layout menu or under Settings → Appearance . Converter. A new module: dates across the solar, Gregorian and lunar calendars, with the days between two dates and adding or taking away days; units in six categories, Iranian units included; and eight size charts for clothes, shoes and rings. Add it from Tools → Modules ; it works fully offline. List cards in their kind's colour. The soft wash the grid tiles carry now sits behind list cards too, so a text, a checklist or a voice note can be told apart at a glance in either layout. Search no longer loses words. Adding a caption, or an edit arriving from another device, could drop the words read from a note's attached photo or file out of search until the note was edited again. Now nothing is dropped, and the first start after this update repairs notes affected before. Persian tags and kinds in search. tag: finds a tag written with the Arabic ک or ی or with different spacing, and type: understands Persian names such as عکس, صوتی or چک‌لیست. A closest match for long notes too. When nothing matches, "The closest thing you wrote" now compares word by word, so a near miss inside a long note or a voice transcript is offered as well. Steadier search results. Searching with filters alone lists notes the way the timeline does — pinned first, then by last change — and a stray half-space or quote mark no longer brings up the whole library. Each keystroke also searches once instead of twice.

item.title: Nex 2.6.29
item.description: No duplicate checklists. If closing the capture box to save a checklist was interrupted after the list was already saved, trying again used to make a second, identical list. It now finds the one already made. A file that could not be saved says so. Picking a file whose copy went missing, or saving onto a full phone, used to fail silently. It now says why, with a retry, as photos do. Smoother typing in the capture box. While you type, Nex no longer reloads the whole timeline behind the box at every pause; it updates once when the box closes. Lighter photos and recordings. Photos kept as taken, extra photos picked with them and finished recordings are saved straight from the file instead of being loaded into memory twice. Widgets in Vazirmatn. On a Persian phone, the home-screen widgets now use the app's own Persian font. The widget picker shows real sample rows for the Timeline and Recap widgets instead of an empty card, the Cycle ring grows with the widget, and the capture buttons respond to touch. A quieter grid. Grid tiles carry only a hint of their kind's colour now, and a day folds away with motion as well as opening with it — by tap or by pinch. A smoother timeline in a big library. Picking a note, a reminder ringing or the daily summary arriving no longer makes Nex regroup every loaded note, and a sideways swipe along the tag row no longer folds the summary or loads older notes. The date under the filters also updates as soon as notes arrive or go.

item.title: Nex 2.6.28
item.description: A better grid view. Card size now applies to the grid: compact fits three tiles to a row, standard and easier to read two. Tiles show more of each note — its words, a checklist's items with their ticks, the photo itself, a voice note's length — and a reminder with its time ("in 3 hours"). Urgent notes carry the same flame as in the list, the colours are calmer, and a day folds and opens smoothly, by tap or by pinch. Show in full no longer appears in a tile's menu, where it had nothing to do. Clearer menu icons. Urgent and Remind now look like Pin in a note's hold menu and its More actions: a filled icon while it is on, an outlined one while it is off. Choose list or grid from the start. The last welcome page asks how you want your notes laid out, as Settings → Appearance does. Coming soon: Converter. A new module on the way, shown under Modules: dates between the Persian, Gregorian and lunar calendars, and weights, lengths, temperatures and clothing, shoe and ring sizes between systems, offline.

item.title: Nex 2.6.27
item.description: Six new themes. Bolder palettes that pair a deep colour with a bright one, each in light and dark: Lavender, Peach & charcoal, Bloom (maroon and mustard), Dusk (plum and peach), Coral and Sunflower (black and yellow). Find them in Settings → Appearance → Theme. A grid view. Settings → Appearance → View → Grid (or Home layout) shows your notes as tiles, two to a row, each in its kind's own soft colour, with the same days, pins and folds as the list. The list stays the default. Pick a note from its icon. Tap the round icon at the start of a card — the mark of its kind — to select it, the way a mail app selects from the avatar; tap it again to put it back. Holding and choosing Select still works. Clearer colours in every theme. A full contrast check of Light, Dark and Night across every palette: the Undo and Got it buttons on the message capsule were too faint to read in all of them and now stand out; filled boxes in the classic light theme, field edges in three palettes, and very bright accent colours you pick now all meet the readability standard. A tidier daily nudge. What is due now reads one item a line, the most pressing first: "Urgent: …", "Today at 10:00 · …", "Overdue: …". It used to be one run-on sentence behind a changing lead-in ("A quick reminder: Urgent: …"). A note written in the other language no longer jumbles its quotation marks, and the expanded notification no longer leaves empty lines under the text — the same goes for note reminders. The greeting above it is now in the app's language too, whatever script your name is written in. Recent searches run again. On the search screen, touching one of your recent or kept searches closed search instead of searching for it. It now runs that search. Exported photos open as the right picture. In a library export, two photos with the same file name were both saved, but the second note's Markdown pointed at the first one's file, so opened outside Nex it showed the wrong photo. Each note now links to its own. Every search box works the same way. The searches in Settings, Modules, What's new, the vault, Words, tags, languages and the rest now share one design: the same look, a clear button as soon as you type that resets the list at once, and Persian or English text running the right way as you type it.

item.title: Nex 2.6.26
item.description: Ready for Android 16. Nex now targets the latest Android. On a tablet or an unfolded foldable it turns with the device instead of staying upright, with the notes kept to a comfortable reading width in landscape; photos taken there are saved the way you held the device. Phones stay in portrait as before. Smoother opening and closing. Opening a note, a page or a menu over the timeline used to rebuild every card on it, and closing it did the same again — the stutter as a note rose and fell. The timeline now stays as it is underneath. The wordmark in the corner now moves only when you touch it, instead of every few seconds on its own. Liquid Glass is paused. It was too heavy for some phones, so its switch has left Settings → Appearance until it is reworked, and the app uses its plain surfaces. A choice you made is kept for when it returns. A pasted address becomes a link. Paste a web address into an empty note with the paste button and the note turns into a link, saved with the page's title and summary instead of as a line of text. Tap Note to keep it as plain text. One name for the daily nudge. Settings, its sound and Android's notification settings now all call it the same thing, in both languages; Android's list no longer switches between two names.

item.title: Nex 2.6.25
item.description: Redesigned themes. Choose from 14 palettes in Settings → Appearance, each with its own light and dark colours. Your saved theme returns automatically, custom accents keep their hue with readable text, and Liquid Glass follows the palette. A scheduled note comes back whole. Sending a note later used to return only its words: the title and the tags it was filed under were dropped while it waited. They come back with it now, and a note that carries files stays in the library instead of being scheduled away from them. Backups survive a wrong clock. If the phone's date moved backwards, automatic backups stopped for as long as it took the clock to catch up, and the copy just written could be treated as the oldest and pruned. Both now behave. Backups without media are refused before restore. Restoring one no longer closes the open library first, only to fail on a file that was never there. And a complete restore that fails no longer leaves a hidden undo step that would roll the library — and everything written after it — back on the next launch.

item.title: Nex 2.6.24
item.description: Liquid Glass now has depth. With the material on, each pane is lit rather than merely tinted: the page's own colour comes through more vividly, a bevel catches the light along the top edge, a soft bounce lifts the bottom edge, and the top bar, dock, menus, dialogs and sheets throw a faint halo onto the page. Dark and Night have their own bounce and warmth, and high contrast still falls back to a solid surface. A reminder marked Done stays answered. If you press Done on a reminder before opening Nex, the daily nudge no longer brings that reminder back on the same day, even when the plan is built as the app starts. The note keeps its due date, so a repeating or future reminder still arrives on time.

item.title: Nex 2.6.23
item.description: Nex opens without the wait. The opening animation used to hold every launch for two seconds, including a tap on the capture widget. It now plays in full only the first time a new version runs; every other launch goes straight from the icon to your notes the moment the library is ready. On this day. On a day with nothing due, the daily nudge can bring back a note you wrote on the same date in an earlier year — "A year ago today you wrote…" — instead of a general line. It follows your calendar (Persian or Gregorian), never uses deleted or set-aside notes, stays entirely on the phone, and has its own switch under Settings → Reminders and notifications.

item.title: Nex 2.6.22
item.description: Reminders from the modules respect the app lock too. With the app lock on, a habit, medication, parking or appointment reminder still showed what it was about on the lock screen; only note reminders were hidden. Every reminder follows the lock now. A habit reminder ticks the right day. One that rang between midnight and your zone's offset from UTC logged its check against the previous day — and Done pressed from the notification could be thrown away as "not today". The day it registers against is now the day it actually rings on. The daily nudge keeps saying something real. A phone that delivers it late — an inexact alarm, a strict battery manager — no longer replaces the day's notes and reminders with a generic line, and a failed delivery no longer costs the day. The notification's channel name also follows the app's language instead of staying in the one it was created in.

item.title: Nex 2.6.21
item.description: Liquid Glass, rebuilt and switched back on. The frosted material behind the top bar, menus, sheets, dialogs and the dock is new: noticeably more of the page's colour comes through, every pane catches a light along its top edge, and Dark and Night have their own tuning so a panel is finally visible against the page behind it. Off by default — turn it on in Settings → Appearance. The glass top bar finally draws. In the retired material the frosted strip behind the title silently rendered at zero height, so the title sat straight on the scrolling notes. It is a real band now, with the same hairline the panes carry.

item.title: Nex 2.6.19
item.description: A snappier library at every size. Saving, editing and deleting a note no longer rereads the whole search index to find the one row it is changing, so every write — a capture, an edit, a tag, a reminder — costs the same on a large library as on a small one. The home screen settles sooner after each change. The tag filter row's live counts, and what is due back from Set aside, are answered from a narrow index built for exactly those questions, rather than by rereading every note in the library. Opening a large library is faster. The index check each open makes now asks its questions of the index's own keys instead of reading every indexed note, and the one-time reorganisation an upgrading library performs takes seconds where it took minutes. Tag-filtered lists and reminders release on time. Lists narrowed by a tag read the tag's own index, and Set-aside notes returning on schedule hand their list back sooner.

item.title: Nex 2.6.18
item.description: More readable surfaces. Stronger contrast for vault bank cards, banners, module icons, tags, switches and urgent markers across Light, Dark and Night. Better Persian typography. More comfortable line height, legible counters and consistently sized attachment badges. Quieter motion when requested. Reduced-motion settings now apply to pages, sheets, camera, onboarding and loading indicators. Clearer, gentler feedback. Unified touch feedback for reminders, checklists and switches; faster banner exits, smoother filters and more efficient reminder-bell animation.

item.title: Nex 2.6.17
item.description: Larger files, clear refusals. Ordinary attachments now allow 500 MB; oversized or unreadable selections explain why they were not imported. Untagged appears only when useful. The filter hides when every timeline note has tags and clears an empty active selection. Undo keeps its promise. Permanent trash deletion waits until its Undo actually closes, and AI edits keep an Undo button in compact editors. Capture preserves unsaved work. Failed writes stop media handoff; failed conversions keep the original reminder and retry without duplicating the converted note. Reminder taps survive the lock. Recurring reminders open their destination after unlocking. Editing continues at the end. Notes, captions and attachment captions open with the caret after the existing text. Assistant answers use real library totals. Counts come from the database; internal searches stay out of replies and interrupted cloud answers get one bounded retry. Bottom navigation is easier to see. A subtle outline and a distinct background separate the dock from content in Light, Dark and Night. Navigation returns quietly after capture. Closing capture restores the dock without the rotation and zoom animation. Restore checks compatibility before changing your library. Older supported libraries are upgraded on a temporary copy; incompatible or malformed backups leave the current library untouched. Interrupted restores keep a recovery path. Library, media and full-backup settings can return to the previous state; cleanup failures after a successful restore no longer report failure or stop the app opening. A healthy backup can repair missing files. Missing photos in the current library no longer prevent restoration, and the safety copy records which files were already missing. Backup files keep their meaning when shared. A library backup renamed to .zip is recognized, and shared rescue backups retain their missing-file report. Invalid appearance settings are rejected before installation.

item.title: Nex 2.6.16
item.description: An Undo can no longer be swallowed silently. A plain banner arriving while an actionable one is still up waits its turn instead of eating it — and a banner replaced by a newer one leaves through the edge it came from, with its exit animation. Banners keep their own time. They arrive in half the time they used to, their words are readable from the first third of the entrance, the countdown starts once the entrance is over, scales with the message's length, and holding a banner pauses it. Sending a note reads as success. The capture sheet leaves as soon as the words are settled — the timeline reloads behind the closing animation — and the send button becomes a ✓ rather than greying the sheet out like a failure. The first keystroke changes no sizes. Paste keeps its column with only its icon fading, and the schedule hint waits for the words to be still, so nothing jumps around under the arriving keyboard. Paste shows when there is something to paste. The sheet asks — without reading the clipboard — on open and on return, so an empty clipboard no longer shows a button that visibly does nothing. A link's Open sits on the toolbar. Each note kind's primary action — Open for links and files, Edit for text — takes the first slot by rank, not by matching translated labels, which is why Open always used to hide behind More. Long notes open the editor full screen. Past about eight lines the editor owns the screen from the start instead of a 220px box, and ✕ and ✓ are its controls in either size. Pickers arrive like the rest of the app. The time and date pickers rise and settle on the app's own beat and scrim rather than Flutter's flat 150ms fade, and the assistant's settings sheet is the app's own sheet again. The camera's wait is spoken. While the sensor is being asked for, the panel shows a faint skeleton and says what it is doing — and six seconds in it offers the phone's camera app, before the timeout does. Covered, not cleared. Pulling the shade over the vault lays a blur across it and comes straight back with the form as it was — words, caret and place — instead of rebuilding it from a draft; being away past the grace period still locks. The assistant hold hint gets a button. "Got it" is a real button now rather than part of the sentence, and the hint keeps to the app's own label style — still shown only when the assistant can actually answer. A toast leaves the way it arrived. Its content's exit — a small settle and fade on the exit token — completes the entrance it always had. A cut preview says so. A multiline bilingual preview that runs out of rows ends in an ellipsis instead of reading as the note's ending, and blank lines are no longer spent from the budget. A fast retreat is not a flick. Pulling back through the middle to cancel a capture flick no longer fires the opposite side's shortcut; the opposite side still works by crossing its full arm. The wide-window scale is said out loud. Appearance now notes that a wide window draws everything at 90% of the chosen size — the factor was always there, silently, on the notes' own text too. One clearance rule for the dock. A single helper reserves the capture dock's room instead of the same sum written out screen by screen, and the dock itself gives way under an open keyboard. Chosen Night hands over in black. With Night chosen, the window between the system splash and the app's first frame is painted black instead of flashing Soft Dark's grey.

item.title: Nex 2.6.14
item.description: Working tag filters in search. The Tags row finally appears in the search filter sheet, typing tag: finds your tags, and several chosen tags now mean "any of them" — the same as the timeline's filter chips. An honest Undo in the trash. Leaving the trash after deleting a note for good no longer leaves an Undo banner that cannot bring it back. Reading an AI answer or a translation no longer closes the note. Scrolling a long result inside its box stays inside the box, instead of taking the whole sheet with it. Delete works from a recurring item's linked notes. Deleting a linked note there now moves it to the trash with an Undo, instead of quietly doing nothing. A friendlier link capture. Pasting text that is not an address no longer dead-ends: Send keeps it as the note it already is and says so, a Clear button appears, and the "not a link" hint waits until you stop typing. The back gesture keeps a recording in progress. Leaving the recording sheet the way Android goes back now keeps the recording — the same as Stop — instead of throwing it away.

item.title: Nex 2.6.13
item.description: Faster opening of long notes and text files. The first page appears with the detail sheet instead of waiting for it to finish opening. Smoother reading and actions. Long documents reveal progressively and keep menus and scrolling more responsive; Markdown blocks and whitespace stay intact.

item.title: Nex 2.6.12
item.description: Smoother returns from Settings and Recurring. Unchanged recurring commitments no longer trigger a full Home screen redraw when closing these pages. Reliable recurring updates. Changes to schedules, completion history and attached details still appear, and today's completion counts refresh correctly after midnight. Smoother navigation throughout Nex. Unchanged screens in Threads, Library, Set Aside, note details, Home layout, and Intelligence no longer redraw unnecessarily after returning. Real changes remain visible. Notes, tags, attachments, and thread membership continue to update when edited.

item.title: Nex 2.6.11
item.description: Smoother return to Home. Closing note details or returning from another page avoids unnecessary timeline rebuilding when nothing has changed. Reliable note updates. Actual changes to notes, reminders, tags and AI-enriched content continue to appear, even while filters are active. Tidier circular note markers. Reminder, urgent and attachment indicators now sit precisely on the main icon's rim rather than overlapping its centre.

item.title: Nex 2.6.10
item.description: Smoother scrolling with long notes. Timeline previews now do far less work when a note contains lengthy text or Markdown, so the list responds more smoothly. Lighter expand and collapse. Opening or closing groups of long notes is faster, without changing the full contents of your notes or their appearance.

item.title: Nex 2.6.9
item.description: Precisely aligned note badges. The centres of tag dots above and attachment, priority and reminder badges below now sit on the full-size note icon's actual circular rim. The main icon stays the same size even with multiple badges, and spacing adapts to the card density. Three tags, without losing your data. New notes cannot take a fourth tag. Older notes keep existing extra tags until you remove them in note details. Imports with more than three distinct tags on a note are rejected before saving any notes, with a clear warning rather than silently discarding tags.

item.title: Nex 2.6.8
item.description: A clearer capture button. The + stays white on Nex blue while custom accent colours keep a legible icon. Clearer timeline cards. Circular note icons now show tag colours above and reminder, urgent and attachment marks below. Selection and ringing reminders use the same circle; selecting a ringing note acknowledges it without deleting its reminder. More readable navigation and filters. Tag filters show quiet note counts, while the floating navigation bar gets a fine outline and soft shadow. Liquid Glass temporarily paused. The option is disabled while its appearance is refined; the saved selection remains intact.

item.title: Nex 2.6.7
item.description: Night is now true OLED black. A pure-black page, charcoal cards and softer text give Night its own quiet look. Light feels calmer. A white page and gentle grey cards make notes easier to scan, without decorative card borders or shadows. Clearer fields and matching Android colours. Text fields keep a slim visible outline; Android launch and home-widget colours follow the new look. Your accent, Liquid Glass and accessibility settings still work.

item.title: Nex 2.6.6
item.description: Soft Dark and a familiar Night. Dark uses calm blue-grey surfaces and softer text, with fewer decorative borders and shadows. Night keeps the former dark look; System follows your device using the new Dark. Existing dark selections become Night. Custom accents and Liquid Glass remain available. A steady Nex appearance. Preset themes are temporarily unavailable while the main Nex look is refined; their saved choices are kept. Correct note order in threads. Notes stay in chronological order even when their saved timestamps have different precision.

item.title: Nex 2.6.5
item.description: Rescue library backups. Keep recoverable notes and files even when some attachments are missing, with a clear missing-file list. Normal backups keep their complete-file checks. More responsive libraries. Capture stays available during sync network waits, and smart search does less repeated work in large libraries. Card status icons sit closer together with a consistent small bottom gap. Complete private-vault backups. Choosing Include private vault now carries its encrypted photos, recordings and files to the restored device. Large private lists and draft saving are lighter. Safer sync and updates. Unsent conflicting edits are kept as a separate note. Approved interrupted downloads can resume after restarting Nex; store copies continue to update only through their store. File saving and scheduled-note processing are more reliable.

item.title: Nex 2.6.4
item.description: Balanced timeline cards. File names and one-line or multiline previews are vertically centred again. Reminder, attachment and urgent icons appear in that order with tiny separate halos that follow the card's press highlight. Reminder times and attachment counts are temporarily hidden on cards; their data and accessible descriptions remain available.

item.title: Nex 2.6.3
item.description: More room for your notes. Timeline previews keep their full width in every card size, including three lines in Large. Reminder, urgent and attachment marks sit over the lower edge with a soft fade, while short notes stay fully visible and captions remain grey.

item.title: Nex 2.6.2
item.description: Uniform timeline cards. Collapsed notes keep one height across text, photos, links, checklists and voice. Captions use a quieter preview line; reminder, urgent and attachment marks stay together in a separate area without empty slots.

item.title: Nex 2.6.1
item.description: A more useful smart summary. Pending work, reminders and important notes take priority; routine completed habits no longer crowd them out. Calmer capture and easier translation. Paste fades smoothly as its space closes, and the whole translation language bar opens the picker. Steadier timeline cards. Reminder, attachment and urgent marks share the preview space on ordinary collapsed cards, while captions and expanded notes keep their room. Optional assistant Memory. Keep a short introduction behind a separate opt-in, with your existing text preserved. Assistant, smart-summary and Memory settings dim when AI is off. One place for AI request history. What left this device stays under Security and privacy. More selective note summaries. Long explanations are condensed instead of merely reformatted, while short or information-dense notes keep the room their facts need. Reliable quick capture. Notification shortcuts open the right capture tool even when the timeline widget is active. Safer photo editing. Clearing all drawings and text now asks for confirmation before removing your work. Control over assistant reads. Reading Recently Deleted or recurring items for an answer waits for your approval. Clearer selected filters. Selected tag labels remain readable in light, dark and Comfort themes, including custom accents.

item.title: Nex 2.6.0
item.description: Easier photo cropping. Larger touch areas make all four crop handles easier to drag while keeping the visible crop controls in place. A clearer assistant history. Conversations are grouped by time with reply previews and a current-chat indicator. Individual deletion is in each conversation’s menu. A steadier pull to refresh. Reversing your drag closes the refresh strip before the notes scroll. A quiet Nex accent marks success, with separate handling for cancelled and failed refreshes. Find notes without tags. Untagged stays at the end of the tag row and works with note-type and reminder filters. More room to write. The capture clipboard fades away once you start writing and gives its space back to the editor; clearing the text brings it back. Clearer recurring cards. Countdown and exact time sit together, with balanced spacing and centred actions. The check button explicitly marks one occurrence done. Captions for text notes. Add a separate optional caption without replacing the note on its timeline card. Captions are included in search and AI context. Mark what is urgent. Use More Actions or the hold menu to add a small flame. Urgency is independent of Pin and keeps notes in their existing order. Daily nudges without AI. Get brief local reminders based on urgent notes, nearby or recently overdue reminders, unfinished checklists and recurring items. A fresh smart summary is optional; otherwise Nex uses local text, with varied prompts for quiet and empty libraries and at most one daily notification.

item.title: Nex 2.5.4
item.description: Clearer note summaries. More compact summaries better preserve decisions, conditions and figures, with readable formatting and a full expanded view. Safer backup restore. Backups made with an unsupported database format are refused before replacing your library. Markdown that comes back cleanly. Re-imported Nex text and checklist exports keep their dates, tags and titles, without metadata or file IDs appearing as note text. Assistant controls that apply throughout. Image and voice settings also govern media sent from the assistant, including changes made while a chat is open. Less work while you type. Short searches stay local; meaning searches wait for a typing pause and cancel superseded requests. Unrelated settings changes no longer rebuild the app's themes.

item.title: Nex 2.5.3
item.description: A visible summary timestamp. The home summary shows how long ago its last successful AI update was, with minutes and hours and an exact time in its tooltip. Relevant habit settings. The habit-sharing option appears only while Habits is active. Portrait rewrites stay visible. Keep reading the current portrait while its replacement is written; the new text and traits appear on the same page. Useful pinned modules. Compact home cards show local progress, review counts, upcoming occasions, the selected breathing session or cycle information in place of large module names. Still, a quieter theme. Warm neutral surfaces and a soft sage accent, in light and dark. Cards, panels and menus have no decorative borders or shadows; focus and error states remain clear. Clearer Markdown conversion. “Convert to Markdown” distinguishes converting a note inside Nex from saving a file to your device. Open PDF and DOCX with Nex. Choose Nex from Android’s Open with menu to keep and read these documents, just like Markdown files. Know when the next turn is. Recurring cards show a countdown and the exact due date and time alongside daily progress, amounts and snooze status when relevant.

item.title: Nex 2.5.2
item.description: Readable wide tables. Markdown and DOCX tables scroll horizontally with readable column widths, while surrounding text stays within the page. Consistent notifications. Opening Nex keeps module notifications in the notification centre. In-app messages use the top capsule throughout Nex, including Undo and retry actions. Notes stay at the heart of your brief. Preset summaries keep useful note content alongside optional habit progress. Full has room for more topics, and Plain report also includes recent notes without reminders.

item.title: Nex 2.5.1
item.description: Habits in your brief, by choice. Opt in to include relevant habit goals, progress and short statistics in the home summary and daily notification. Switching it off hides previous habit content while keeping the notes summary and independent reminders. Useful habit reminders. See which habit is due, mark a tick done, open an amount's progress form, or ask for a reminder later. Notifications open the right place. Module notifications lead to their item or relevant section, including when Nex was closed, while respecting the app lock. Consistent home AI. Greetings follow the app language even after a failed request. Changing the brief's length or style applies on return from settings, without waiting for the hourly refresh. Better AI editing. item.title: Nex 2.3.5
item.description: Clouds that drift in. In pull to refresh, a cloud now drifts in from beyond the edge instead of appearing inside the sky, and the drift runs as one smooth, endless loop — it no longer jumps every few seconds. A copy made for Cafe Bazaar and Myket. The copy published for the stores has no in-app updater and no longer asks for permission to install apps, because the store keeps it up to date. No unencrypted connections at all. The installed app now refuses unencrypted (http) connections everywhere; the one exception, for developers' own test machines, is left in development builds only. item.title: Nex 0.7.8
item.description: The top section (the first ## heading, whatever it is titled) is exactly what release.yml publishes as the GitHub Release body — and exactly what the in-app update sheet then shows. That is the whole mechanism: no separate changelog service, no template rendered at request time. Working convention: Add each user-facing change as a short bullet under Unreleased , in the same pull request that makes the change. If it does not change anything a user would notice, it does not belong here — that is what the commit history is for. When cutting a release, rename ## Unreleased to ## vX.Y.Z (matching the tag about to be pushed) and start a fresh ## Unreleased above it for whatever comes next. release.yml refuses to publish if the top section is still literally titled Unreleased — that heading has to be renamed first, every time.
